findings.title: The published wrong-password case requires an invocation witness that never records P3 calls
findings.finding: p3PublishedLogin(LOGIN,true) snapshots REPLAY_INVOCATIONS and requires containsExactly("fill", "click"). The unchanged /invocation handler appends only when asynchronousPage || observedChoicePage. Both default to false; the referenced old fixtures restore them to false, and p3Case never enables them or another P3 recording condition. Thus genuine P3 native fills/clicks are forwarded by the existing worker tap but discarded by the HTTP witness. The new published wrong-password test necessarily reaches this assertion with an empty list if its preceding checks pass; the empty-list assertions for the other P3 branches are also vacuous as invocation evidence.
findings.requestedChange: Add a P3-scoped invocation witness at the existing forwarding seam and use its per-case delta, preserving the old nine fixture behavior and original invoke call exactly once. Do not enable old asynchronous/choice page behavior to make this assertion pass.
findings.validationBoundary: Static contradiction in the reviewed source; no runtime was executed.

findings.title: The published registration control does not check its actual FINAL outcome for unwanted annotation
findings.finding: The registration branch tests public report.errorCode and report.detail, then skips p3RunnerReport entirely. The adjacent failure branch explicitly documents that runner causes live in the authenticated FINAL outcome rather than public errorCode. A PASSED FINAL that incorrectly retains outcome.errorCode=LOGIN_REQUIRED or outcome.detail therefore can satisfy the registration assertions while the public API omits those fields. This fails to prove the requested passing/no-annotation control at the actual runner boundary.
findings.requestedChange: Inspect the captured successful registration FINAL through p3RunnerReport, retain execution/attempt/admission/instance/sequence identity checks, and assert the actual outcome has no errorCode/detail annotation plus passing original step receipts. Keep the accepted public FAILED/errorCode-null vocabulary unchanged.
findings.validationBoundary: Missing assertion on the actual captured outcome; no invented API mapping or runtime claim.

findings.title: Owned ordinary executions are not cancelled or settled before fixture state is cleared on failure
findings.finding: p3Execute creates a genuine accepted ordinary execution and puts it only in the class-wide P3_EXECUTIONS callback-capture set. p3Case finally cleans testOwnedSessions (guided sessions) only; the referenced AfterEach also cancels only guided sessions. If p3AssertBinding or dispatchOnce fails after acceptance, the ordinary execution can remain queued; if p3AwaitExecution times out, it can remain active. Finally then clears APP mode, native sessions, credentials and entitlement fixtures without settling that owned execution. A queued execution can contaminate the next dispatchOnce count, and an active execution can continue against cleared fixture authority.
findings.requestedChange: Track each case’s accepted ordinary executions separately and use genuine bounded cancellation/terminal acknowledgement before restoring APP/Core/entitlement state. Preserve the primary error with suppressed cleanup failures and prevent later case execution when owned teardown remains unconfirmed.
findings.validationBoundary: Concrete failure paths in new helpers; this is bounded test resource ownership, not a broader process/revocation or lifecycle review.

findings.title: Unexpected successful negative starts fail before their session can be tracked for cleanup
findings.finding: p3Call asserts the expected HTTP status before parsing/tracking an actual successful guided start, and tracking additionally depends on the requested status being 202. If either the mayUse denial or missing-scope refusal regresses to a real 202, the helper throws immediately and leaves the returned session absent from testOwnedSessions. Neither p3Case nor the existing failure cleanup can cancel that session. The denied-principal case also needs the actual owning cookie retained for a legitimate cancellation; the default P3 cookie belongs to user-1.
findings.requestedChange: Record any actual successful guided-start response and its actual owning identity/cookie before asserting the expected refusal status. Clean that unexpected owned session through the genuine authenticated route with bounded teardown and retain the original refusal assertion as the primary failure.
findings.validationBoundary: Concrete negative-test regression path; no simulated cancellation or ownership bypass is requested.
